title: MicroscopeSketch: Accurate Sliding Estimation Using Adaptive Zooming

problem.claim: High-accuracy real-time data stream estimation is needed for various applications, particularly with sliding-window techniques.

gap.claim: Current methods have difficulty providing high accuracy, broad applicability, and low memory consumption at the same time.

contributions.claim: MicroscopeSketch is a high-accuracy sketch framework for sliding estimation.
Adaptive zooming dynamically adjusts counter granularity to maximize accuracy while minimizing memory usage.
MicroscopeSketch is applied to frequency estimation, top-k frequent-item discovery, and top-k heavy-change identification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report substantial improvements over existing methods across three tasks.
The authors report roughly fourfold error reduction for frequency estimation.
The authors report roughly threefold error reduction for identifying top-k items.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-time data stream estimation is important, and sliding-window techniques have received attention.
Existing solutions do not simultaneously provide high accuracy, generality, and low memory usage.
The paper presents MicroscopeSketch and its adaptive-zooming technique for adjusting counter granularity.
The framework is evaluated on three estimation and discovery tasks, with reported error reductions over existing methods.
The relevant source code is reported as available in a GitHub repository.

source_observation.claim: Counter granularity is dynamically adjusted during sketch-based estimation.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive resource allocation may help balance estimation accuracy against memory usage.

application.claim: Consider adaptive precision or granularity for streaming systems with competing accuracy and memory requirements.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this tradeoff applies beyond the reported tasks or workloads.

unknowns: Specific datasets, workloads, and baselines are not described.
Exact memory usage, latency, accuracy metrics, and experimental conditions are not reported.
The GitHub repository location and reproducibility details are not provided in the source units.
